What does carpet installation cost in Bothell, WA?

Plan on $4 to $7 per square foot installed in Bothell — that covers carpet, pad, labor, new tack strip and haul-away. Most projects here total $2,000 to $4,500, and a 1,200 sq ft main floor with a staircase generally falls between $5,500 and $8,500. The grade you pick moves the price more than anything else, and you pick it from samples laid out in your own rooms.
Does the mobile carpet showroom come to Bothell?

It does — both sides of the county line. The van brings 20+ carpet samples and all three pad grades to your Bothell address, whether that's a Canyon Park cul-de-sac or a townhome near Main Street. We set samples down in the rooms they'd go in, measure the whole job, and leave a written price behind. The appointment costs nothing.
What does carpet stretching cost in Bothell?

Stretching starts at $99 per room in Bothell. A power stretcher pulls the slack out of rippled, wavy carpet and flattens trip spots, usually for about one-fifth of what replacement would run. If the pile still stands up and the color still works for you, stretching is almost always the smarter spend.
What do carpeted stairs cost in Bothell?

Stair work starts at $18 per step, done waterfall or cap-and-band. Bothell's two-story stock from the 80s and 90s means we quote plenty of staircases — landings and pie-shaped winders go into the written number from the start, so nothing shows up as a surprise line later.
How long does a carpet install take in a Bothell home?

One day covers most Bothell homes. Three or four rooms plus a staircase is a comfortable single day for the crew; a full house with heavy furniture or several flights can spill into a second. Your quote states the schedule in writing, so you know before install day rather than during it.
Will your installers move my furniture?

Yes. On most jobs the crew moves the big pieces — beds, couches, dressers, tables — and puts each one back once the carpet is in. Your part is the small stuff: closet floors, electronics, breakables and anything personal you'd rather carry yourself.
Should I stretch my Bothell carpet or replace it?

Stretch when the pile still stands, the backing is sound and the color still suits the room — that's a $99-per-room fix instead of a full recarpet. Replace when traffic lanes are crushed flat, seams are opening, the backing is separating, or pet odor has outlived professional cleaning. We look first and tell you which side you're on before writing the quote.
Which parts of Bothell do you cover?

All of them — Downtown, Canyon Park, Thrashers Corner, North Creek, Fitzgerald, Norway Hill, Westhill, Shelton View, Maywood Hills, Queensgate, Waynita and Bloomberg Hill, on both the King and Snohomish County sides. We also carpet homes in Kenmore, Woodinville, Mill Creek, Brier and the rest of the Northshore area.
What carpet holds up best with dogs and cats?

Solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing, installed over a moisture-barrier pad. The color runs through the fiber, so it tolerates diluted bleach without fading, and the barrier pad keeps accidents from soaking into the subfloor — the source of odor that never leaves. The barrier pad upgrade starts at $0.65 per square foot.
What warranty comes with the installation?

OC Flooring backs the workmanship with a 1-year warranty, and the carpet carries the manufacturer's mill warranty on top — typically 10 to 25 years on wear and stain depending on grade. Both appear in writing on your quote. Pad choice can affect mill coverage, which is one reason all three pad grades ride along on the visit.
